rules.basis: The generator sheets print one cell 'Watts (Starting/Running)' as '5000/4000', the starting watts first; the column is in watts. The unqualified cell is the gasoline rating: a dual-fuel sheet labels its LPG and natural-gas cells, and the 201534 sheet prints the same figures under 'GASOLINE WATTS'.
The dual-fuel sheets print the same cell per fuel, the fuel in the name, whose first figure is the starting watts.

The GB225 manual prints the gasoline cell as 'Manual Watts (Starting/Running)', '5000/4000', beside its LPG and NG cells; the 201223 sheet from the same source gives 4000 W under 'Gasoline Watts', so the cell is the gasoline rating, starting first.
The same cell's second figure is the GB225's running watts on gasoline.
The same cell's second figure is the running watts on gasoline. 'Rated Power' and 'Power' are not read: on one sheet they equal the running watts and on another the starting watts.
The dual-fuel sheets print the same cell per fuel, the fuel in the name, whose second figure is the running watts.
The home standby sheets state the continuous power per fuel in kilowatts, 22 on LPG and 19.8 on natural gas, the fuel in the name.
The generator sheets state 'Gasoline Capacity' as '2.25 gal. (8.50 L)' or as a bare '5' or '4.7' on a US sheet whose column is in gallons; the fuel is in the name.

The generator sheets state the output as 'Volts AC' or 'AC Volts', '120' or '120/240', and the standby sheets as 'Rated voltage' '120/240', both alternatives of one output; the same name on the power station is its inverter's.
The 100113 water pump sheet states its flow as 'Max Delivery Volume', '158 gal/min (598 L/min)'.

The 100113 water pump manual states 'Total Head' as '98 ft. (29.9 m)', the height it lifts against; on another sheet the name could be an operating point, so the rule reads that manual only. 'Suction Head' is the lift on the inlet side and is not read.
